title: Bhagavad Gita: A Thematic Learning Path
description: A lesson-based introduction to the Bhagavad Gita, organized by ideas and supported by chapter and verse references.

sections.title: Arjuna's Grief
sections.subtitle: A crisis becomes a question
sections.description: Meet Arjuna on the battlefield as concern for family, duty, and the consequences of violence overwhelm him. Notice how admitting confusion opens the way to learning.
learning_objectives: Recognize Arjuna's conflict
Explain why he asks Krishna for guidance
Distinguish grief from a considered resolution

questions.prompt: What most directly causes Arjuna to hesitate before the battle?
options: He sees teachers, relatives, and friends among those assembled
He has forgotten how to use his bow
He does not know where the battlefield is
He wants to become king immediately
questions.correct_answer: He sees teachers, relatives, and friends among those assembled
questions.explanation: Arjuna's distress grows as he recognizes loved ones and respected elders on both sides.

questions.prompt: What does Arjuna do after explaining his doubts to Krishna?
options: He asks Krishna to guide him
questions.correct_answer: He asks Krishna to guide him
questions.explanation: His request for instruction marks the shift from argument toward a student seeking counsel.

questions.prompt: Arjuna's first reaction is a calm, detached analysis of his duty.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The opening chapter depicts a deeply personal emotional crisis; reflective instruction follows.

sections.title: The Eternal Soul
sections.subtitle: What changes, and what does not
sections.description: Explore Krishna's teaching that the embodied self is distinct from the changing body, and consider how this view reframes loss and change.
learning_objectives: Summarize the body and self distinction
Interpret the clothing metaphor
Connect impermanence with perspective

questions.prompt: In Krishna's teaching, what changes while the self is described as enduring?
questions.correct_answer: The body
questions.explanation: Krishna compares bodily change to changing garments while describing the self as enduring.

questions.prompt: What does the image of changing clothes illustrate?
options: The embodied self moves on from an old body to a new one
questions.correct_answer: The embodied self moves on from an old body to a new one
questions.explanation: The clothing image in BG2.22 compares the discarded body to worn garments.

questions.prompt: Krishna describes the self as something that weapons can destroy.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: BG2.23 says the self is not destroyed by weapons, fire, water, or wind.

sections.title: Act Without Attachment
sections.subtitle: Give your effort; release your grip
sections.description: Learn the Gita's influential teaching on action: attend to the work you can do without making its reward the sole measure of your choices.
learning_objectives: State what is within one's control
Distinguish nonattachment from inaction
Apply the teaching to an everyday task

questions.prompt: According to BG2.47, what is within your control?
options: Your action, not a guaranteed result
questions.correct_answer: Your action, not a guaranteed result
questions.explanation: The verse directs attention to action without claiming ownership over its fruits.

questions.prompt: Nonattachment to results means a person should stop acting altogether.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The teaching calls for responsible action without fixation on reward; it does not praise idleness.

questions.prompt: A student prepares carefully for an exam but cannot control the questions or final score. Which response best reflects BG2.47?
options: Do the preparation sincerely and accept that the score is not fully controllable
Refuse to study because results are uncertain
Study only if a top score is guaranteed
questions.correct_answer: Do the preparation sincerely and accept that the score is not fully controllable
questions.explanation: The practical focus is sincere effort, while recognizing that outcomes depend on more than one's effort alone.

sections.title: The Steady Mind
sections.subtitle: Wisdom in the middle of change
sections.description: Meet the sthitaprajna, the person of steady wisdom, and examine the Gita's account of desire, attention, and inner balance.
learning_objectives: Identify qualities of steady wisdom
Trace how attachment can grow into distress
Choose a pause before reacting

questions.prompt: How does Krishna describe a person of steady wisdom when desires arise?
options: They are not ruled by every desire and remain inwardly composed
questions.correct_answer: They are not ruled by every desire and remain inwardly composed
questions.explanation: BG2.55 describes one who gives up compulsive desires and is content in the self.

questions.prompt: What chain does BG2.62-63 warn can begin with dwelling repeatedly on an object?
questions.correct_answer: Attachment, desire, and eventually confusion
questions.explanation: The verses trace how repeated contemplation can lead through attachment and desire toward anger and loss of discernment.

questions.prompt: Equanimity in BG2.56 means never feeling anything.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: The teaching concerns steadiness amid pleasure and pain, rather than emotional numbness.

sections.title: Duty and Selfless Service
sections.subtitle: Work that serves beyond the self
sections.description: See why action is unavoidable and how work performed with care and without selfish attachment can support a wider good.
learning_objectives: Explain why inaction is not the answer
Describe action as service
Reflect on one's responsibilities

questions.prompt: Why does Krishna say that a person cannot remain completely inactive?
options: Everyone is impelled to act by qualities of nature
questions.correct_answer: Everyone is impelled to act by qualities of nature
questions.explanation: BG3.5 notes that no one can remain actionless, even for a moment.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes action performed as yajna in BG3.9?
options: It is offered in a spirit of service rather than selfish attachment
It is done only for praise
questions.correct_answer: It is offered in a spirit of service rather than selfish attachment
questions.explanation: BG3.9 contrasts action tied to sacrifice or service with action that binds through selfish attachment.

questions.prompt: A team member quietly handles an important task that helps the whole group. What best reflects selfless service?
options: Do the task responsibly without making recognition the only goal
Avoid the task unless everyone notices
Take credit for another person's work
questions.correct_answer: Do the task responsibly without making recognition the only goal
questions.explanation: Selfless service values responsible contribution while loosening the demand for personal reward.

sections.title: Knowledge and Renewal
sections.subtitle: Wisdom transforms action
sections.description: Explore the transmission of yoga, Krishna's account of restoring dharma, and the role of knowledge in freeing action from confusion.
learning_objectives: Recognize the teacher and student lineage
Summarize the purpose of divine descent
Connect knowledge with wise action

questions.prompt: Why does Krishna say he appears age after age?
options: To protect the good, restrain harmful forces, and re-establish dharma
questions.correct_answer: To protect the good, restrain harmful forces, and re-establish dharma
questions.explanation: BG4.7-8 describes divine manifestation in relation to dharma and the protection of beings.

questions.prompt: In BG4.34, how is knowledge approached?
options: With humility, inquiry, and service to those who know
questions.correct_answer: With humility, inquiry, and service to those who know
questions.explanation: BG4.34 names respectful approach, sincere questions, and service as ways to learn from the wise.

questions.prompt: BG4.38 presents knowledge as a powerful purifier over time.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: Krishna calls knowledge supremely purifying and says it is found in time by one perfected in yoga.

sections.title: Training the Mind
sections.subtitle: Practice and patient return
sections.description: Learn the Gita's practical response to a restless mind: repeated practice, detachment, and patient redirection.
learning_objectives: Describe the mind as both support and obstacle
Name two supports for steadiness
Practice returning attention without self-judgment

questions.prompt: What two supports does Krishna name for mastering the restless mind?
questions.correct_answer: Practice and detachment
questions.explanation: BG6.35 acknowledges the mind is difficult to control but says it can be restrained through practice and detachment.

questions.prompt: When attention wanders during meditation, what does BG6.26 advise?
options: Bring it back and place it again on the self
Follow every thought to its end
questions.correct_answer: Bring it back and place it again on the self
questions.explanation: The practice is to notice wandering and gently return the mind to the intended focus.

questions.prompt: BG6.5 encourages a person to uplift themselves through the mind.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: The verse presents the mind as capable of serving as one's friend or one's obstacle.

sections.title: Devotion in Daily Life
sections.subtitle: Offer what you have, with care
sections.description: Study devotion as remembrance, offering, and a way of meeting ordinary actions with sincerity and care.
learning_objectives: Recognize the value of a sincere offering
Identify qualities of a devoted person
Connect remembrance with everyday action

questions.prompt: What does BG9.26 say Krishna accepts when offered with devotion?
options: A leaf, flower, fruit, or water
questions.correct_answer: A leaf, flower, fruit, or water
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes the loving devotion with which a simple offering is given.

questions.prompt: How does BG9.27 invite a person to approach daily activity?
options: Offer actions, food, and efforts to the divine
Keep daily actions separate from values
questions.correct_answer: Offer actions, food, and efforts to the divine
questions.explanation: The verse extends offering to ordinary actions, eating, giving, and disciplined effort.

questions.prompt: Which quality appears among those dear to Krishna in Chapter 12?
questions.correct_answer: Kindness toward all beings
questions.explanation: Chapter 12 describes the devotee as friendly and compassionate, among other qualities.

sections.title: Seeing the Divine
sections.subtitle: The many and the one
sections.description: Follow Arjuna's request to see Krishna's universal form and reflect on how the Gita presents the divine presence throughout existence.
learning_objectives: Understand why Arjuna asks for a vision
Recognize the universal form as encompassing all existence
Reflect on humility before the vast

questions.prompt: Why does Arjuna ask Krishna to reveal the universal form?
options: He wants to directly witness Krishna's cosmic nature
He wants to end the dialogue
He wants to test his bow
He asks for a map of the battlefield
questions.correct_answer: He wants to directly witness Krishna's cosmic nature
questions.explanation: After hearing Krishna's teachings, Arjuna asks to see the divine form directly, if Krishna considers him able.

questions.prompt: What does Arjuna's vision of the universal form communicate?
options: The divine form encompasses the many dimensions of the cosmos
The universe is limited to one family
questions.correct_answer: The divine form encompasses the many dimensions of the cosmos
questions.explanation: Chapter 11 depicts a form containing countless beings and aspects of the universe.

questions.prompt: Arjuna sees the universal form using only ordinary vision.
questions.correct_answer: False
questions.explanation: Krishna grants Arjuna divine vision to behold the form.

sections.title: Choice and Surrender
sections.subtitle: Understand, reflect, then choose
sections.description: Reach the dialogue's close: Krishna offers instruction, Arjuna reflects, and the learner is invited to act with understanding and resolve.
learning_objectives: Recognize the place of reflection and choice
Summarize the dialogue's resolution
Connect learning with a considered next step

questions.prompt: After teaching Arjuna, what does Krishna invite him to do in BG18.63?
options: Reflect on the teaching and then act as he chooses
questions.correct_answer: Reflect on the teaching and then act as he chooses
questions.explanation: Krishna tells Arjuna to reflect fully on the teaching and then do as he wishes.

questions.prompt: What change does Arjuna express near the end of the Gita?
options: His delusion is gone and he will act according to Krishna's word
He asks to return to sleep
questions.correct_answer: His delusion is gone and he will act according to Krishna's word
questions.explanation: In BG18.73 Arjuna says his delusion has been destroyed and that he will act with resolve.

questions.prompt: The Gita ends with Sanjaya describing the dialogue and its significance.
questions.correct_answer: True
questions.explanation: Sanjaya closes the text by recalling the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna.
